title: A year of bench lots
summary: Nineteen sample roasts, four that made the shelf, and one that we are still arguing about.
body:
A bench lot is a kilo of something we are not sure about, roasted on the sample machine and put in front of whoever is in the building.

Nineteen of them this year. Four made it onto the shelf, including the Bolivian that turned into the cascara work. Eleven were fine and unremarkable, which is the usual outcome and not a waste of anybody's morning.

Four were bad. Two were our fault — one scorched, one baked so flat it tasted of cardboard — and two were green coffee that no roast profile was going to rescue.

The one we are still arguing about is a natural from Uganda that half the room called a fruit bomb and the other half called a wine gum. It is not on the shelf. It may yet be.
